body.statement: For every \(P\in\mathcal M_{K,\varepsilon}\), \(\phi_j=U_j-\psi_j\) is an observed-data influence function for \(\psi_j\); it is the static, zero-discount specialization of the categorical product-bridge construction in Appendix A.8 of Bian, Zhou, and Cui.
body.justification: The finite projection needs a valid starting gradient whose relationship to published categorical bridges is exact.
body.gap: Bian, Zhou, and Cui provide validity but not canonicality for the present static continuous-outcome target.
body.consumer: It lets analysts retain the multiply robust bridge architecture while replacing its avoidable variance by the canonical correction.
body.proof_tex:
Fix a target class \(j\).  Invertibility of the two measurement matrices gives
\[
E\{a_j(A,X)\mid J=\ell,X\}=E\{z_j(Z,X)\mid J=\ell,X\}=\mathbf 1\{j=\ell\}. \tag{25}
\]
Conditional independence then implies
\[
E(\phi_j\mid J=\ell,X)=m_j(X)-\psi_j. \tag{26}
\]
For a factorwise centered latent score, (25)--(26) give, term by term,
\[
\begin{aligned}
E(\phi_js_X)&=E[(m_j(X)-\psi_j)s_X(X)],\\
E(\phi_js_\pi)&=0,\\
E(\phi_js_Y)&=E\!\left[\frac{\mathbf 1(J=j)}{\pi_j(X)}\{Y-m_j(X)\}s_Y(Y,J,X)\right],\\
E(\phi_js_A)&=E(\phi_js_Z)=0.
\end{aligned} \tag{27}
\]
The first and third lines are exactly the derivatives of \(E_Pm_j(X)\) with respect to the \(X\)-marginal and the class-\(j\) outcome law; the other factor derivatives are zero.  The differential-score lifting theorem represents every observed DQM score by such a centered additive latent score.  Since \(\phi_j\) is observed measurable, iterated expectation and (27) prove the influence-function equation for every observed path.  Its mean is zero by (26), and bounded \(Y\), latent positivity, and the two inverse-matrix bounds give \(\phi_j\in L^2(P)\).

Appendix A.8 of Bian, Zhou, and Cui defines inverse features whose conditional expectations are latent-category indicators and multiplies two such features in its categorical influence function.  Setting its discount to zero and identifying reward with \(Y\), surrogate with \(A\), and the second proxy with \(Z\) gives exactly (25) and the displayed \(U_j\); this verifies the stated specialization independently of the preceding validity proof.
